Hi Sally — great to hear the pilot went well. Short answer: we can be flexible for pilot engagements but there are a few constraints to balance with operational guarantees. Proposed compromise we can take to legal today: 

1) Pilot exception: for pilot orders <= $50k ARR we can accept a 60-day auto-renew opt-out (meaning either party can terminate the subscription with 60 days prior written notice). We generally default to 90 days for standard commitments, but can make a one-time concession for pilots to 60 days.

2) Termination for convenience: Redwood is comfortable with a TFC right for pilots limited to the initial 6-month pilot period only. TFC would carry a 60-day notice and Redwood would refund pre-paid, unused committed capacity on a pro-rata basis less any usage true-up. We cannot accept an unlimited unilateral TFC for committed, multi-year reserved capacity without additional termination fees.

3) Offboarding: we'll provide a staged offboarding playbook (attached) that guarantees data export within 7 business days including a standard export package. For keys: we support customer-managed KMS on private deployments; for hosted accounts we'll provide an export and documented key rotation/handling steps.

I've attached a candidate redline of the MSA (redline_msa_v3.docx) with language that captures the pilot carveouts and the staged offboarding schedule. Looping in Laura and Karthik to weigh in on the legal and procurement impacts.

If that looks reasonable to Acme, we'll update the order form and send the DocuSign package for signature.

Thanks,
Markus Klein

Markus / Karthik — reviewing Markus' proposed language. A few legal points and suggested edits (see redline_msa_v3.docx):

- Scope of pilot carveout: make the 60-day termination and adjusted auto-renew explicitly conditional on order form language (i.e., "Pilot Order Form - Pilot Amount <= $50,000"). This avoids a permanent change to our global auto-renew policy.

- TFC cap: add a liability/payment floor for early termination if customer terminates during active committed capacity periods (e.g., refund only up to pre-paid usage; reserved capacity commitments beyond pilot remain chargeable).

- Staged offboarding: propose three phases — (A) notification and handoff window (0-14 days), (B) export and validation (15-30 days), (C) final wipe and closure (31-60 days). This gives operations a buffer and maps to support SLAs. Language: "Customer shall be provided with a copy of Customer Data and reasonable assistance to transition services in accordance with the Offboarding Playbook."

- Data export timing: 7 business days for a standard export is fine for small pilots, but require language that allows up to 14 business days for exports that exceed X GB or require manual processing. Include measurement threshold.

- KMS / keys: for hosted clients include the standard clause that we will provide a documented export and signing key rotation plan; for Private deployments we note KMS option. Do not promise custody of customer keys for hosted accounts.

I'll attach a short paragraph we can push to Acme to preserve our reserved capacity protections while granting the pilot concession. Once Markus gets an affirmative from Acme, I'll prepare a final redline and the e-sign package.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
